raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Fixes #43139. General plugins can provide weight placement without wrapping private `ModelRunner.load_model` internals. This is independent of #43597.

## Modifications

- Add a public factory receiving frozen `OffloaderContext`. Return a runner-specific `BaseOffloader`, or `None` for native selection.
- Retain each runner's offloader. For targets, call `post_load_model` after platform processing and `post_init`, before subsequent model setup and memory sizing. Validate its returned module and release the temporary load-result reference. Drafts keep their existing `wrap_modules`-only lifecycle.
- Reject active providers combined with native offload flags or startup weight-loading overlap: overlap materializes final weights after this hook. Factory and placement failures stop initialization.
- Keep DeepGEMM's shared copy-engine choice conservative across live offloaders, so draft construction cannot erase a target's restriction. Track policies weakly without retaining them solely for this check.
- Document the entry point, lifecycle and replacement responsibilities; add registered CPU coverage.

## Accuracy Tests

45 CPU tests passed: 21 new and 24 existing.

| Test file | Passed |
| --- | ---: |
| `test/registered/unit/utils/test_offloader.py` | 13 |
| `test/registered/unit/model_executor/test_model_runner_offloader.py` | 8 |
| `test/registered/unit/model_executor/model_runner_components/test_startup_weight_load.py` | 22 |
| `test/registered/unit/spec/test_plugin_hook_signatures.py` | 2 |

Lifecycle tests call the real `ModelRunner.load_model` with loading/device helpers mocked, checking ordering, replacement, draft isolation, failure propagation and model lifetime.

Single-L4 live-server checks passed with Qwen3-0.6B, Torch 2.14.1+cu130, TP=1 and CUDA Graphs disabled. With no provider, an identity provider, and a CPU-offloading provider, three prompts per configuration produced identical text, token IDs and token log probabilities (72 generated token positions per configuration; maximum difference `0.0`, fixed tolerance `1e-3`). All measured requests followed HTTP readiness and completed built-in warmup, using seed 0.

The offloading provider relocated 276,861,440 bytes of CUDA parameters. `max_total_num_tokens` was 131,703 with no provider and with the identity provider, versus 134,135 with offloading (+2,432). This checks that the real KV budget reflects placement in this fixture; it is not an arbitrary-model accuracy or capacity guarantee.

A separate single-L4 comparison tested native `--cpu-offload-gb 1` against the plugin's late `OffloaderV1` placement with the same 1-GiB limit, Qwen3-0.6B and TP=1. Both captured a full decode CUDA Graph for batch size 1, with eager prefill, and completed 69 measured target-decode replays after readiness. Three prompts produced identical text, token IDs and log probabilities (24 tokens each; maximum difference `0.0`, fixed tolerance `1e-3`). Parameter layouts and placement matched: 880,932,864 CPU bytes and 311,166,976 CUDA bytes; both reported `max_total_num_tokens=139,922`. This validates the two tested placement paths, not arbitrary-provider equivalence.

<details>
<summary>Validation scope and limitations</summary>

- Base `f9cee8d2b2d96a626db1968ba81e4d72bb31794a`. CPU: Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and the upstream optional kernel-import stub; the project pins Torch 2.14.1. Subsequent Python formatting preserved the ASTs.
- Live probes use `PythonTreeCore` in every arm because a matching Rust extension for this base was unavailable. These do not validate the default Rust-backed tree path.
- The initial live comparison failed the fixed tolerance: maximum token-log-probability difference `0.0466426611`. Logs showed the first measured request overlapping built-in warmup; causation is unproven. The passing follow-up corrected readiness and fixed seed 0, retaining the production patch, checker and tolerance.
- All tracked files passed applicable pre-commit hooks, excluding branch protection and four Rust hooks; no Rust changes. Final documentation also passed applicable hooks. The documented example and Mintlify 4.2.1002 `validate` passed; link checking had the same 737 existing errors on base and patched trees.
- Prefill CUDA Graphs, multi-GPU execution, DeepGEMM GPU execution and FlexTensor integration remain untested. Decode-graph evidence is limited to the explicit full-graph, batch-size-1 configuration above.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No throughput or latency claim. The measured placement/KV result above is a small integration check. The conservative DeepGEMM policy check is not performance-benchmarked.

- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). Limited live comparison is reported above; no task-accuracy or speed benchmark was run.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -878,6 +878,103 @@ sglang serve --model-path <model> [options]
 # Look for "Scheduler initialized!" in logs
 ```
 
+### Weight placement providers
+
+An SRT general plugin can register a weight offloader without replacing private
+model-loading methods. Use `register_offloader_factory` from
+`sglang.srt.utils.offloader` during plugin registration. Each worker process
+accepts one factory: registering the same callable again is harmless; registering
+a different callable raises an error.
+
+The factory receives an `OffloaderContext`, a frozen `msgspec.Struct` with
+runner-local fields:
+
+| Field | Meaning |
+| --- | --- |
+| `device: str` | Runner device type, such as `cuda` or `cpu` |
+| `gpu_id: int` | Runner device index |
+| `tp_rank: int` | Tensor-parallel rank |
+| `model_config: ModelConfig` | This runner's model configuration |
+| `is_draft_worker: bool` | Whether the runner loads a speculative draft model |
+
+Return a fresh `BaseOffloader` instance for each runner, or `None` to use SGLang's
+native offloader selection for that runner. The context's fields cannot be
+reassigned; this does not make the referenced `model_config` deeply immutable.
+Copy-engine eligibility is conservative across the process: if any live offloader
+returns `True` from `forbid_copy_engine_usage`, the shared copy-engine path is
+unavailable to other runners too. Separate instances do not imply support for
+concurrent or reentrant model construction.
+
+For example, create `my_weight_plugin/__init__.py` with this no-op provider:
+
+```python
+from sglang.srt.utils.offloader import (
+    BaseOffloader,
+    OffloaderContext,
+    register_offloader_factory,
+)
+
+
+class PlacementOffloader(BaseOffloader):
+    def __init__(self, context: OffloaderContext):
+        self.context = context
+
+    def post_load_model(self, model):
+        # Finalize your target model's placement here.
+        return model
+
+
+def create_offloader(context: OffloaderContext):
+    return PlacementOffloader(context)
+
+
+def register():
+    register_offloader_factory(create_offloader)
+```
+
+Use this `pyproject.toml` beside the package directory, then install the package
+with `pip install -e .` in your SGLang environment:
+
+```toml
+[build-system]
+requires = ["setuptools"]
+build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"
+
+[project]
+name = "my-weight-plugin"
+version = "0.1.0"
+
+[project.entry-points."sglang.srt.plugins"]
+weight_placement = "my_weight_plugin:register"
+```
+
+This example leaves placement unchanged and uses the device selected by your
+existing SGLang launch configuration. If you filter general plugins with
+`SGLANG_PLUGINS`, include `weight_placement`.
+
+For a target runner, SGLang calls the provider's `post_load_model(model)` once,
+after the platform's `post_load_model` and the offloader's `post_init`, but before
+profiling hooks, weight-memory measurement, KV-cache sizing, and CUDA Graph
+capture. It must return a `torch.nn.Module`; the default returns the input model.
+Returning the same model preserves its identity. If you return a replacement,
+you must preserve the model interface and any references or hooks installed by
+the loader or platform. Draft runners use the provider's `wrap_modules` during
+construction but do not call its `post_init` or `post_load_model`.
+`wrap_modules` runs once per `make_layers` stack; its `submodule_accessor` and
+`whitelist_param_names_creator` arguments may be `None`.
+
+The plugin owns tensor relocation and the forward behavior needed to use those
+tensors. Moving weights to CPU alone does not provide on-demand GPU transfers or
+guarantee a larger KV cache. Validate inference and memory accounting for each
+supported model and platform.
+
+An active provider cannot be combined with `--cpu-offload-gb` greater than zero,
+`--offload-group-size` greater than zero, or `--startup-weight-load-mode=overlap`.
+These checks apply only when the factory returns a provider; returning `None`
+retains native behavior. Factory and `post_load_model` exceptions abort runner
+initialization. General-plugin discovery and registration retain their existing
+error-handling policy, so inspect startup logs to confirm your plugin registered.
+
 ### Hook Types
 
 `HookRegistry` supports four hook types:
